Yes—probably, though it may take a little effort.

A **58% illuminated Moon**, **31° above the horizon**, and about **99° from the Sun** is generally visible to unaided eyes in a clear daytime sky. Its large separation from the Sun helps, and at that altitude it avoids the worst horizon haze.

Look toward the **southwest**, at an azimuth of about **232°**—roughly **52° west of due south**—and about **31° up**. Shield your eyes from direct sunlight and use a building edge or other landmark to help focus at the right distance. Once found, it should be reasonably easy to keep seeing.

So under the clear conditions you describe, I’d expect you to have a **good chance of spotting it**.
